_comment: Flipkart - a second MARKETPLACE feed, in the SAME shape as amazon_marketplace.json. Identical columns on purpose: agent/sources.py already speaks this format, so this whole vendor integration is four lines (FlipkartAdapter - a key, a display name, a path). That is the adapter layer's claim, shown rather than asserted. It is the same trick PackHub/OfficeStock and BoxBazaar/TradeBridge already demonstrate: three formats, six vendors, and the normalising code written once per format.
_pairs_note: Several listings here are the SAME PHYSICAL PRODUCT as a listing in amazon_marketplace.json, described completely differently and priced slightly apart. That is the point of having both files: FLK-LAP-2101 'Dell 15 Laptop 11th Gen - Carbon Black' and AMZ-LAP-1101 'Dell Inspiron 15 3520 15.6" FHD Laptop (12th Gen Core i5-1235U/8GB DDR4/512GB SSD...)' are one machine. Nothing downstream compares titles - after normalisation both carry 8GB RAM and 512GB SSD, both fail a 16GB brief for the same stated reason, and the cheaper of the two wins on the price term if they ever qualify. The pairs are: AMZ-PKG-1001/FLK-PKG-2001, AMZ-LAP-1101/FLK-LAP-2101, AMZ-LAP-1102/FLK-LAP-2102, AMZ-FUR-1201/FLK-FUR-2201, AMZ-HPH-1301/FLK-HPH-2301.
_delivery_note: Quoted to a Chennai 600001 buyer, same as the Amazon feed, which is why the same product can be four days from one warehouse and eighteen from another.
_history_note: Authored demo data, labelled 'simulated market data' in the UI. Last reading of each series equals the listing's current price_display / in_stock.
